summary: Hans Windisch (1881–1935) was a scholar in religious studies. He held posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (circa 1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (1939–1999) worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded as Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indologist. He studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctorate under the supervision of Ernst Waldschmidt.

Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal (1884–1939) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Delhi and later at SOAS University of London from circa 1927 to 1932.

Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) was a scholar of archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin, he held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, Heidelberg University, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

Haraprasad Shastri (1853–1931) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Presidency College and Sanskrit College. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and later chaired Bengali and Sanskrit at the University of Dhaka.

Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indologist who studied under H. M. Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ramakant Tripathi, completing his doctorate under Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. Educated at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at both institutions before holding posts at the University of Dhaka (1921) and Banaras Hindu University (1947).
Haridas Sinharay is an Indologist who held a post at Maulana Azad College, attested in 1970 and 1990.

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Muni Jinavijaya. He held academic positions at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the International School of Dravidian Linguistics, and directed the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Harjit Singh is a Tibetologist who held a professorship at Jawaharlal Nehru University, attested in 1997 and 2016.

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies, history, and Indology. Educated at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, he was appointed to the Chair of Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia.
Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was a linguist who served as Director at the University of Mysore (circa 1961–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin (1926–2016) was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University. He taught at Columbia University and Yale University (1962–1996), also serving as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History.

Harold G. Coward (born 1936) is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate from McMaster University in 1973. He held posts as professor at the University of Calgary and director at the University of Victoria.

Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an archaeologist and Indologist. After serving as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar, he held positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Following teaching posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was a long-time humanities professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1970–2013).
Harold Stewart (1916–1995) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney (circa 1939–1941).
